title: kbid.py add fills licence and reuse from the source's own licence record, and suggests the host's usual pair only as a marked guess
goal: kbid.py add, when --licence and --reuse are omitted, reads the licence from the source itself by its family: an arXiv abstract page's licence link (CC BY, CC BY-SA: copy; CC BY-NC-SA, CC BY-NC-ND and the arXiv non-exclusive licence: quote), a GitHub or GitLab repository's licence through its API (an SPDX id: copy, unless NC, ND or source-available: quote), a Microsoft Learn page through its public mirror repository named in the page's github_feedback_content_git_url (kb/_self/content-rules.md, Licensing and privacy), and the fixed pairs of code.claude.com and anthropic.com; for any other host it prints the host's most common pair in _sources.csv marked 'check' and writes nothing until the flags are given; explicit flags always win; the suite tests each family with stubbed responses, never the network.

notes: Premise (2026-10-11, over kb/public/_sources.csv, 3,150 rows): the most common (licence, reuse) pair per host covers 58% of the rows on hosts with two or more rows, the most common reuse class 81%; learn.microsoft.com alone holds 116 distinct pairs because a Learn page's licence follows its public mirror repository, so a host default is wrong too often to write unasked. Today kbid.py add requires --licence and --reuse and a session copies a same-host pair from rag.py src by reading. arXiv licence links were read mechanically from the abstract pages in this session's research (11 papers, five licence kinds). Planned 2026-10-12: premise reproduced (kbid.py add declares --licence and --reuse required=True).
